findings.current: Unnamed wasn’t the only one left speechless by the question.
findings.defect: The reaction’s subject is reversed. The source says Taekyung was not the only person dumbfounded by Unnamed’s words; it does not say Unnamed was also left speechless.
findings.rationale: The construction “나뿐만이 아니었다” explicitly centers Taekyung and indicates that Jeok Cheongang shared his incredulous reaction.
findings.replacement: I wasn’t the only one dumbfounded by Unnamed’s words.
findings.source: 무명의 말에 어이가 없어진 건 나뿐만이 아니었다.

findings.defect: Jeok Cheongang’s spoken threat is converted into an italicized thought and reverses who is about to receive the beating.
findings.rationale: In context, “일단 맞자” is Jeok Cheongang telling the attacker to take a beating immediately before he punches Moon Beauty Saber away.
findings.replacement: “…Let’s start with you taking a beating.”

findings.current: From the perspective of the Murim practitioners gathered there, it was a single punch they had never seen before—and would never see again.
findings.defect: The draft changes an imperceptibly fast punch into one that the spectators merely will not see again in the future.
findings.rationale: “볼 수도 없었던” means they could not see the punch, describing its speed and their inability to perceive it, not its future uniqueness.
findings.replacement: The punch was something none of the martial artists gathered there had seen—or had even been capable of seeing.
findings.source: 이 자리에 모인 무림인들의 입장에서는 본 적도 없고, 볼 수도 없었던 일권(一拳).

findings.current: “Then why did you swing your saber at me without so much as a word?”
findings.defect: The draft adds Taekyung as the target of the saber attack, although the fight and the surrounding exchange were between the Thunderbolt Saber King and Jeok Cheongang.
findings.rationale: The source leaves the object unstated. Adding “at me” contradicts the scene’s established participants.
findings.replacement: “Then why did you suddenly start swinging your saber?”

findings.current: Hong Dao, his close friend, had left behind only one Disciple. To the Thunderbolt Saber King, Unnamed was a particularly painful spot.
findings.defect: The established title “Dharma King” is omitted, and the literal rendering “a particularly painful spot” obscures the idiom’s meaning that Unnamed inspires special concern and protectiveness.
findings.rationale: “아픈 손가락” refers to someone whose circumstances make them an object of particular concern or sympathy, while “법왕” explicitly identifies Hong Dao as the Dharma King.
findings.replacement: Unnamed, the only Disciple left behind by his close friend the Dharma King Hong Dao, was someone the Thunderbolt Saber King couldn’t help but feel protective of.
findings.source: 절친한 벗이었던 법왕 굉도가 남긴 유일한 제자는 그에게 있어 아픈 손가락이었다.

findings.current: “Is that really what the man who burned down Mount Jiuhua and killed a thousand members of the Demonic Cult would say?
findings.defect: The draft makes Jeok Cheongang the person who burned Mount Jiuhua. The source says he killed a thousand Demonic Cult members because they had burned it.
findings.rationale: The causal construction “구화산 태워 버렸다고 … 죽인” assigns the burning to the Demonic Cult members and their deaths to Jeok Cheongang.
findings.replacement: “Is that really coming from the man who killed a thousand members of the Demonic Cult because they burned down Mount Jiuhua?
findings.source: “……구화산 태워 버렸다고 마교도 천 명을 죽인 그 인간이 하는 말이 맞나?

summary: Six actionable fidelity defects, including altered subjects, attack targets, combat mechanics, hierarchy, and causality.
